claim: Cerebellar granule cells constitute the majority of neurons in the brain.
source: Cerebellar granule cells constitute the majority of neurons in the brain and are the primary conveyors of sensory and motor-related mossy fiber information to Purkinje cells.
evidence: This is supported by citations in the manuscript text and represents established scientific knowledge about brain composition.

claim: Granule cells are the primary conveyors of sensory and motor-related mossy fiber information to Purkinje cells.
source: Cerebellar granule cells constitute the majority of neurons in the brain and are the primary conveyors of sensory and motor-related mossy fiber information to Purkinje cells.
evidence: This represents established knowledge about cerebellar circuitry.

claim: Individual granule cells receive mossy fiber inputs from both sensory (upper body proprioceptive) and basilar pontine pathways.
source: Using cell-type-specific projection mapping with synaptic resolution, we observed the convergence of separate sensory (upper body proprioceptive) and basilar pontine pathways onto individual granule cells and mapped this convergence across cerebellar cortex.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The convergence of ECN and BPN pathways onto granule cells has a reproducible, region-specific cerebellar topography.
source: Using cell-type-specific projection mapping with synaptic resolution, we observed the convergence of separate sensory (upper body proprioceptive) and basilar pontine pathways onto individual granule cells and mapped this convergence across cerebellar cortex.
evidence: This is supported by the mapping data presented in Figures 3-5 showing regional variation in convergence patterns.

claim: The multimodality of mammalian granule cells substantiates their associative capacity predicted in the Marr-Albus theory of cerebellar function.
source: These findings inform the long-standing debate about the multimodality of mammalian granule cells and substantiate their associative capacity predicted in the Marr-Albus theory of cerebellar function.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental findings in relation to theoretical predictions.

claim: The convergent basilar pontine pathways carry corollary discharges from upper body motor cortical areas.
source: We also provide evidence that the convergent basilar pontine pathways carry corollary discharges from upper body motor cortical areas.
evidence: This is supported by the retrograde and anterograde tracing data presented in Figure 6.

claim: Merging of corollary and sensory streams is a critical component of circuit models of predictive motor control.
source: Such merging of related corollary and sensory streams is a critical component of circuit models of predictive motor control.
evidence: This represents established theoretical knowledge about motor control systems.

claim: The cerebellum is critical for coordinating movement and for learning sensorimotor relationships.
source: The cerebellum is critical for coordinating movement and for learning sensorimotor relationships (Ito, 2006, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work and represents established knowledge.

claim: Sensory and motor-related afference to the cerebellum is largely conveyed by mossy fiber inputs to granule cells.
source: Sensory and motor-related afference to the cerebellum is largely conveyed by mossy fiber inputs to granule cells, which notably constitute over half the neurons of the mammalian brain (De Schutter and Bjaalie, 2001; Herculano-Houzel and Lent, 2005; Watson et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations and represents established anatomical knowledge.

claim: Granule cells have on average only four dendrites.
source: Granule cells are simple neurons, having on average only four dendrites, each of which receives a single, large, excitatory mossy fiber input (Gray, 1961; Eccles et al., 1967; Palay and Chan-Palay, 1974; Jakab and Hamori, 1988).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior anatomical studies.

claim: Each granule cell dendrite receives a single, large, excitatory mossy fiber input.
source: Granule cells are simple neurons, having on average only four dendrites, each of which receives a single, large, excitatory mossy fiber input (Gray, 1961; Eccles et al., 1967; Palay and Chan-Palay, 1974; Jakab and Hamori, 1988).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior anatomical studies.

claim: Knowing whether multiple types of mossy fibers synapse onto the same granule cell is key to understanding the types of operations they perform.
source: Knowing whether multiple types of mossy fibers synapse onto the same granule cell is key to understanding the types of operations they perform (Ekerot and Jorntell, 2008; Arenz et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations and represents a key conceptual point in the field.

claim: A unimodal granule cell may serve to filter noise by requiring the summation of inputs in order to fire action potentials.
source: For example, a granule cell receiving all synaptic inputs from the same mossy fiber source (i.e., 'unimodal') may serve to filter noise by requiring the summation of inputs in order to fire action potentials (Jorntell and Ekerot, 2006; Ekerot and Jorntell, 2008; Bengtsson and Jorntell, 2009).
evidence: This is a theoretical interpretation supported by citations to prior work.

claim: A multimodal arrangement of granule cell inputs enables more complex functions than a unimodal arrangement.
source: A multimodal arrangement, in which an individual granule cell mixes inputs from different mossy fiber origins (e.g., one sensory and one motor-related precerebellar nucleus), enables more complex functions.
evidence: This is an inference based on theoretical considerations about information processing.

claim: Mixing of mossy fiber inputs was a critical aspect of the expansion recoding of cerebellar afference performed by granule cells in the Marr-Albus theory.
source: Such mixing of mossy fiber inputs was a critical aspect of the expansion recoding of cerebellar afference performed by granule cells in the influential Marr-Albus theory of cerebellar function (Marr, 1969; Blomfield and Marr, 1970; Albus, 1971).
evidence: This is supported by citations to the original theoretical papers.

claim: Electrophysiological evidence was found for multimodal granule cells in the electrosensory lobe of the mormyrid fish.
source: Electrophysiological evidence was found for multimodal granule cells in the electrosensory lobe of the mormyrid fish (Sawtell, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Recent mammalian granule cell input structure studies have failed to positively identify more than one input source converging onto individual cerebellar granule cells.
source: Such studies in the mammal have failed to positively identify more than one input source converging onto individual cerebellar granule cells (Jorntell and Ekerot, 2006; Arenz et al., 2008; Bengtsson and Jorntell, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior electrophysiological studies.

claim: The lack of evidence for multimodality has led to a diminution of models of granule cell function from a recoder to a noise filter.
source: This lack of evidence for multimodality has led to a diminution of models of granule cell function from a recoder to a noise filter (Ekerot and Jorntell, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation and represents a shift in theoretical interpretation.

claim: Previous electrophysiological studies did not systematically examine granule cells across cerebellar cortex.
source: However, these electrophysiological studies did not systematically examine granule cells across cerebellar cortex, nor did they test the most numerous mossy fiber inputs, those originating from the basilar pontine nucleus (BPN) (Brodal and Bjaalie, 1992).
evidence: This is a critique of prior studies based on their methodological limitations.

claim: The most numerous mossy fiber inputs originate from the basilar pontine nucleus (BPN).
source: However, these electrophysiological studies did not systematically examine granule cells across cerebellar cortex, nor did they test the most numerous mossy fiber inputs, those originating from the basilar pontine nucleus (BPN) (Brodal and Bjaalie, 1992).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior anatomical work.

claim: The majority of BPN input originates from output messages of the cerebral cortex, superior colliculus, red nucleus, and other motor centers.
source: The majority of BPN input originates from output messages of the cerebral cortex, superior colliculus, red nucleus, and other motor centers (Burne et al., 1981; Mihailoff et al., 1989; Panto et al., 1995; Schwarz and Thier, 1999; Leergaard et al., 2000; Leergaard, 2003; Tziridis et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior anatomical studies.

claim: BPN mossy fibers are in a position to carry copies of motor commands—corollary discharges—into the cerebellum.
source: Therefore BPN mossy fibers are in a position to carry copies of motor commands—corollary discharges—into the cerebellum (Sperry, 1950; von Holst and Mittelstaedt, 1950; Poulet and Hedwig, 2007; Glickstein and Doron, 2008; Sommer and Wurtz, 2008).
evidence: This is an inference based on the anatomical connectivity, supported by citations to corollary discharge literature.

claim: Corollary discharges are found in circuits involving the intersection of motor and sensory pathways in the central nervous system.
source: In the central nervous system, corollary discharges are found in circuits involving the intersection of motor and sensory pathways (Wolpert and Miall, 1996; Sommer and Wurtz, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations and represents established knowledge about corollary discharges.

claim: The external cuneate nucleus (ECN) projects forelimb and upper-trunk proprioceptive information to the cerebellum.
source: To test both the multimodal nature of granule cells and their specific role in merging pontine and sensory streams, we examined the intersection of the BPN pathway and a primary sensory precerebellar pathway related to motor output—forelimb and upper-trunk proprioceptive information projecting to the cerebellum through the external cuneate nucleus (ECN) of the hindbrain (Campbell et al., 1974; Akintunde and Eisenman, 1994; Quy et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior anatomical studies.

claim: The Slc17a7 gene exhibits regional selectivity for both the ECN and the BPN.
source: The solute carrier family 17 (sodium-dependent inorganic phosphate cotransporter), member 7 (Slc17a7) gene was selected and a knock-in mouse, Slc17a7-IRES-Cre, expressing Cre under the control of this locus was generated.
evidence: This is supported by the experimental data showing selective expression in these nuclei.

claim: The Cre-dependent reporter expression in the Slc17a7-IRES-Cre mouse recapitulates the selective expression pattern of the Slc17a7 locus as reported in the Allen Institute Anatomic Gene Expression Atlas database.
source: The Cre-dependent reporter expression in this mouse recapitulates the selective expression pattern of the Slc17a7 locus as reported in the Allen Institute Anatomic Gene Expression Atlas database (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by comparison with database information and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: ECN inputs primarily project to the ipsilateral cerebellar vermis.
source: As has been previously reported, at a gross level the ECN and BPN target mostly non-overlapping regions of the cerebellum (Akintunde and Eisenman, 1994; Serapide et al., 1994, 2001). ECN inputs primarily project to the ipsilateral cerebellar vermis and BPN inputs bilaterally terminate in the cerebellar hemispheres (Figure 1C,D).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work and confirmed by the imaging data in Figure 1C,D.

claim: BPN inputs bilaterally terminate in the cerebellar hemispheres.
source: As has been previously reported, at a gross level the ECN and BPN target mostly non-overlapping regions of the cerebellum (Akintunde and Eisenman, 1994; Serapide et al., 1994, 2001). ECN inputs primarily project to the ipsilateral cerebellar vermis and BPN inputs bilaterally terminate in the cerebellar hemispheres (Figure 1C,D).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work and confirmed by the imaging data in Figure 1C,D.

claim: ECN and BPN axons co-terminate in many areas of the cerebellum including the vermis, lateral vermis, simple lobule, paraflocculus, Crus1, Crus2, paramedian lobule, and copula of the pyramis.
source: Such areas include the vermis, lateral vermis, simple lobule, paraflocculus, Crus1, Crus2, paramedian lobule, and copula of the pyramis (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by the imaging data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Within co-termination areas, ECN and BPN axons terminate within very close proximity (<50 µm), well within the length of the dendritic arbors of granule cells.
source: Within these areas, ECN and BPN axons terminate within very close proximity (<50 µm), well within the length of the dendritic arbors of granule cells (Figure 1D, inset).
evidence: This is supported by the high-resolution imaging data shown in Figure 1D inset.

claim: A mossy fiber terminal synapses with granule cell dendrites within a glomerulus.
source: A mossy fiber terminal synapses with granule cell dendrites within a glomerulus (Ekerot and Jorntell, 2008; Arenz et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations and represents established anatomical knowledge.

claim: Inside a glomerulus, the claw-footed dendrites of granule cells wrap around and make multiple synaptic contacts with the single, large, mossy fiber termination.
source: Inside a glomerulus, the claw-footed dendrites of granule cells wrap around and make multiple synaptic contacts with the single, large, mossy fiber termination.
evidence: This represents established anatomical knowledge about glomerular structure.

claim: The synaptic arrangement in glomeruli allows determination with light microscopy whether ECN and BPN mossy fibers converge onto single granule cells.
source: This synaptic arrangement allows us to determine, with light microscopy, whether ECN and BPN mossy fibers converge onto single granule cells.
evidence: This is an inference based on the anatomical structure and the resolution of the imaging technique.

claim: The TCGO mouse line expresses tetracycline transactivator and mCitrine in a subset of granule cells.
source: This screen identified one mouse line, TCGO, which expresses tetracycline transactivator and mCitrine in a subset of granule cells.
evidence: This is supported by the experimental characterization of the mouse line.

claim: The density of labeled cells in TCGO mice is consistent across animals.
source: While the density of labeled cells is consistent across TCGO animals, we lack evidence to distinguish if the labeling is stochastic or marks a particular class of granule cells.
evidence: This is based on observations across multiple animals.

claim: 40% of proprioceptive granule cells (2429/5997 in two animals) made obvious synapses with both ECN and BPN inputs.
source: Based on results from one annotator, 40% of proprioceptive granule cells (2429/5997 in two animals) made obvious synapses (see 'Materials and methods') with both ECN and BPN inputs (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the anatomical analysis shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Subsets of ECN and BPN information streams converge at their first opportunity in the cerebellum—onto granule cells.
source: Therefore, subsets of ECN and BPN information streams converge at their first opportunity in the cerebellum—onto granule cells.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the anatomical convergence data.

claim: The pattern and percentage of granule cell types largely agreed across animals and annotators.
source: Both mouse brains were examined by two annotators; the pattern and percentage of granule cell types largely agreed across animals and annotators (Figures 3–5).
evidence: This is supported by the comparative data shown in Figures 3-5.

claim: Some cerebellar areas, such as medial vermis, are composed mostly of E and E+ granule cells.
source: We observed three types of granule cell terrain across cerebellar areas. Some cerebellar areas, such as medial vermis, were composed mostly of E and E+ granule cell (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: This is supported by the mapping data shown in Figure 3A,B.

claim: Vermal areas harbor proprioceptive pathways which are segregated from BPN inputs at the cellular level.
source: Therefore, vermal areas harbor proprioceptive pathways which are segregated from BPN inputs at the cellular level; this segregation would not be evident with traditional neuro-anatomical techniques.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the cellular-level mapping data.

claim: Lateral vermis, simple lobule, copula of the pyramis and Crus1 intermingle all three granule cell types.
source: Other areas intermingle all three granule cell types, this category includes lateral vermis, simple lobule, copula of the pyramis and Crus1 (Figure 4).
evidence: This is supported by the mapping data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Paramedian lobule, the paraflocculus, and Crus2 are dominated by EB granule cells.
source: Lastly, some cerebellar areas are dominated by EB granule cells. These areas include paramedian lobule, the paraflocculus, and Crus2 (Figure 5).
evidence: This is supported by the mapping data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Paramedian lobule, paraflocculus, and Crus2 are 'hotspots' for the intersection of ECN and BPN pathways.
source: These areas are 'hotspots' for the intersection of ECN and BPN pathways, where the majority of proprioceptive granule cells also receive BPN inputs.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the quantitative mapping data showing high EB percentages in these regions.

claim: Differences in the extent and patterns of ECN and BPN convergence suggest that the cerebellum handles proprioceptive information with regional specificity.
source: Differences in the extent and patterns of ECN and BPN convergence suggest that the cerebellum handles proprioceptive information with regional specificity.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the regional variation in convergence patterns.

claim: ECN inputs carry forelimb and upper body proprioceptive information to cerebellar granule cells.
source: ECN inputs carry forelimb and upper body proprioceptive information to cerebellar granule cells (Campbell et al., 1974; Akintunde and Eisenman, 1994; Quy et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior anatomical and physiological studies.

claim: Nearly every paramedian, proprioceptive granule cell receives BPN inputs.
source: We focused on the paramedian lobule as the projection target since nearly every paramedian, proprioceptive granule cell receives BPN inputs.
evidence: This is based on the mapping data showing high EB percentages in the paramedian lobule.

claim: EGFP-labeled neurons were restricted to lateral agranular cortex, consistent with M1 identity.
source: EGFP-labeled neurons were restricted to lateral agranular cortex, consistent with M1 identity (Figure 6B) (Tennant et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by the imaging data in Figure 6B and citation to prior work on M1 anatomy.

claim: The majority of pontine inputs to the paramedian lobule originate from the medial-ventral BPN.
source: The majority of pontine inputs to the paramedian lobule originate from the medial-ventral BPN (Figure 6C, upper).
evidence: This is supported by the retrograde labeling data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Retrogradely-labeled BPN neurons are situated in dense fields of M1 axons.
source: Retrogradely-labeled BPN neurons are situated in dense fields of M1 axons (Figure 6C, lower; Figure 6D).
evidence: This is supported by the imaging data shown in Figure 6C and 6D.

claim: Cortical axons containing presynaptic vesicle proteins were in close proximity to retrogradely labeled pontine neurons.
source: Cortical axons containing presynaptic vesicle proteins (Bellocchio et al., 1998) were in close proximity to retrogradely labeled pontine neurons; these M1 terminals were also associated with post-synaptic densities of BPN neurons (Naisbitt et al., 1999) (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is supported by the immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 6E and citations to marker papers.

claim: Putative M1 synaptic inputs were identified on rabies-labeled BPN neurons in 3/3 animals.
source: Putative M1 synaptic inputs were identified on rabies-labeled BPN neurons (minimum 10 synaptic partners analyzed per mouse) in 3/3 animals.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the anatomical analysis.

claim: Forelimb/upper body pathways separately carrying corollary discharges and proprioceptive information are aligned in cerebellar cortex.
source: Therefore, forelimb/upper body pathways separately carrying corollary discharges and proprioceptive information are aligned in cerebellar cortex.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the combined anatomical tracing data.

claim: Axonal connections carrying pontine information directly converge with proprioceptive pathways onto individual granule cells.
source: Our results indicate that axonal connections carrying pontine information directly converge with proprioceptive pathways onto individual granule cells.
evidence: This is the primary finding of the study supported by the anatomical data.

claim: The percentage of proprioceptive granule cells exhibiting convergence with BPN inputs varied across cerebellar areas.
source: The percentage of proprioceptive granule cells exhibiting such convergence varied across cerebellar areas.
evidence: This is supported by the regional mapping data in Figures 3-5.

claim: These findings establish the multimodal nature of granule cells.
source: These findings establish the multimodal nature of granule cells and locate a merging of sensory and corollary pathways in specific cerebellar subregions.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the convergence data as evidence for multimodality.

claim: The findings locate a merging of sensory and corollary pathways in specific cerebellar subregions.
source: These findings establish the multimodal nature of granule cells and locate a merging of sensory and corollary pathways in specific cerebellar subregions.
evidence: This is supported by the regional mapping and M1 tracing data.

claim: David Marr and James Albus proposed that by mixing mossy fiber inputs, granule cells could perform 'expansion recoding', enabling them to contribute to pattern separation and motor learning.
source: David Marr and James Albus proposed that by mixing mossy fiber inputs, granule cells could perform such 'expansion recoding', enabling them to contribute to pattern separation and consequently to be fundamental for motor learning (Marr, 1969; Blomfield and Marr, 1970; Albus, 1971).
evidence: This is supported by citations to the original theoretical papers.

claim: In the Marr-Albus model, the associative capacity of granule cells is maximized if different modalities of mossy fibers are mixed onto individual granule cells.
source: In this model, the associative capacity of granule cells is maximized if different modalities of mossy fibers are mixed onto individual granule cells.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the Marr-Albus theory.

claim: Jorntell and Ekerot's failure to find evidence for mixing in the C3 region led them to disfavor the multimodal view and relegate granule cell function from expansion recoding to noise reduction.
source: In the C3 region of the anterior paravermis of the cerebellum, failure to find evidence for mixing led Jorntell and Ekerot to disfavor the multimodal view and relegate granule cell function from expansion recoding to noise reduction (Jorntell and Ekerot, 2006; Ekerot and Jorntell, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work and represents a shift in interpretation.

claim: Reassignment of granule cell function from expansion recoding to noise reduction implies a marked reduction in the pattern discrimination capability of the cerebellum.
source: Such reassignment of function implies a marked reduction in the pattern discrimination capability of the cerebellum.
evidence: This is an inference about the computational implications of the functional reassignment.

claim: Arenz et al. provided indirect evidence for multimodal inputs to three granule cells in the cerebellar flocculus.
source: In the cerebellar flocculus, Arenz et al. (2008, 2009) provided indirect evidence for multimodal inputs to three granule cells.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Both previous electrophysiological mapping experiments failed to test the convergence of pontine and sensory pathways because they were performed in animals where the cortico-ponto-cerebellar pathway was either interrupted or suppressed.
source: Relevant to our study, both of these electrophysiological mapping experiments failed to test the convergence of pontine and sensory pathways because they were performed in animals where the cortico-ponto-cerebellar pathway was either interrupted or suppressed.
evidence: This is a critique of prior studies based on their methodological limitations.

claim: The current analysis has yielded the first direct evidence that a large number of mammalian cerebellar granule cells receive inputs from both pontine and primary sensory sources.
source: This analysis has yielded the first direct evidence that a large number of mammalian cerebellar granule cells receive inputs from both pontine and primary sensory sources.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the findings supported by the anatomical data.

claim: The results provide a map of where multimodal convergence occurs and does not occur over the expanse of the cerebellar cortex.
source: Our results also provide a map of where this variety of multimodal convergence occurs and does not occur over the expanse of the cerebellar cortex.
evidence: This is supported by the comprehensive mapping data in Figures 3-5.

claim: Multimodal claw-footed granule cells have been observed in the electrosensory lobe of the mormyrid fish.
source: Multimodal claw-footed granule cells have also been observed in the electrosensory lobe of the mormyrid fish, suggesting multimodality is a feature of this morphological cell type that is conserved across vertebrate species and across brain regions (Sawtell, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Multimodality is a feature of claw-footed granule cells that is conserved across vertebrate species and across brain regions.
source: Multimodal claw-footed granule cells have also been observed in the electrosensory lobe of the mormyrid fish, suggesting multimodality is a feature of this morphological cell type that is conserved across vertebrate species and across brain regions (Sawtell, 2010).
evidence: This is an inference based on observations in multiple species and brain regions.

claim: The labeling strategy rarely accounted for all presynaptic partners of an individual granule cell.
source: The observation that our labeling strategy rarely accounted for all presynaptic partners of an individual granule cell suggests that multimodality is likely a more prevalent feature of cerebellar granule cells than indicated by the convergence of the ECN and BPN pathways reported here.
evidence: This is based on observations during the anatomical analysis.

claim: Multimodality is likely a more prevalent feature of cerebellar granule cells than indicated by the convergence of the ECN and BPN pathways.
source: The observation that our labeling strategy rarely accounted for all presynaptic partners of an individual granule cell suggests that multimodality is likely a more prevalent feature of cerebellar granule cells than indicated by the convergence of the ECN and BPN pathways reported here.
evidence: This is an inference based on the incomplete labeling of inputs.

claim: The associative capacity of the cerebellum is thought to largely depend on Purkinje cell plasticity.
source: The associative capacity of the cerebellum is thought to largely depend on Purkinje cell plasticity, allowing temporal relationships among inputs to alter the strengths of postsynaptic responses (Marr, 1969; Albus, 1971; Boyden et al., 2004; Gao et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations and represents established theory about cerebellar learning.

claim: Unimodal granule cells supply segregated input channels to Purkinje cells, allowing the molecular layer to independently adjust the weights of each modality.
source: Unimodal granule cells supply segregated input channels to Purkinje cells, allowing the molecular layer to independently adjust the weights of each modality.
evidence: This is an inference about the computational implications of unimodal inputs.

claim: Multimodal granule cells suggest that some parallel fiber inputs already represent information types.
source: In addition to this independent modality control, the present finding of multimodal granule cells suggests that some parallel fiber inputs already represent information types.
evidence: This is an inference about the computational implications of multimodal inputs.

claim: Prefabricating simple associations in granule cells may enable Purkinje cells to perform more complex learning operations, analogous to the enhanced learning capacity of a multilayer perceptron over a single layer perceptron.
source: Prefabricating simple associations in granule cells may enable Purkinje cells to perform more complex learning operations, analogous to the enhanced learning capacity of a multilayer perceptron over a single layer perceptron (Minsky and Papert, 1969).
evidence: This is a speculative inference drawing an analogy to machine learning theory.

claim: Motor control systems require knowledge of the environment, the position of the body, and how it moves to perform skilled behaviors.
source: In order to perform skilled behaviors, motor control systems require knowledge of the environment, the position of the body, and how it moves.
evidence: This represents general knowledge about motor control.

claim: Proprioception is particularly well suited to provide input to the brain's sensory model of body position and kinematics by signaling muscle stretch and tendon tension.
source: By signaling muscle stretch and tendon tension, proprioception is particularly well suited to provide input to the brain's sensory model of body position and kinematics (Bosco and Poppele, 2001; Dietz, 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations and represents established knowledge about proprioception.

claim: Many behaviors require predicting the likely consequences of a motor plan prior to, or without, movement.
source: Proprioceptive and other sensory afferents deliver accurate post-hoc reports of movements, but many behaviors require predicting the likely consequences of a motor plan prior to, or without, movement (Wolpert and Miall, 1996; Bastian, 2006; Shadmehr et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations and represents established knowledge about motor control.

claim: Forward models use information about intended movements to predict the likely consequences of a voluntary action.
source: Forward models have been proposed to use information about intended movements to predict the likely consequences of a voluntary action (Robinson, 1975; Jordan and Rumelhart, 1992; Wolpert and Miall, 1996).
evidence: This is supported by citations and represents established theory about motor control.

claim: Forward models require two inputs: sensory inputs that update the state of the model and corollary discharge signals related to intended actions.
source: Forward models require two inputs: sensory inputs (peripheral afference) that update the state of the model and corollary discharge signals related to intended actions.
evidence: This represents established theory about forward models.

claim: To predict sensory consequences, corollary discharges are thought to mimic self-generated (reafferent) sensory information.
source: To predict sensory consequences, corollary discharges are thought to mimic self-generated (reafferent) sensory information.
evidence: This represents established theory about corollary discharges.

claim: Where and how corollary discharges are converted from motor to sensory coordinates in the nervous system is largely unknown.
source: To accomplish this mimicry, corollary discharges must be converted from motor to sensory coordinates, but where and how this occurs in the nervous system is largely unknown.
evidence: This represents a gap in current knowledge.

claim: Theory and perturbation studies suggest somatic forward models reside in the cerebellum.
source: Theory and perturbation studies suggest somatic forward models reside in the cerebellum (Miall et al., 1993, 2007; Miall, 1998; Wolpert et al., 1998; Blakemore et al., 2000; Pasalar et al., 2006; Ebner and Pasalar, 2008; Ito, 2008; Lesage et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to theoretical and experimental work.

claim: Proprioceptive and corollary discharge pathways converge on individual granule cells.
source: We show that proprioceptive and corollary discharge pathways converge on individual granule cells.
evidence: This is the primary finding of the study supported by the anatomical data.

claim: Granule cells can generate action potentials in response to a single mossy fiber input.
source: Granule cells can generate action potentials in response to a single mossy fiber input (Rancz et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior physiological work.

claim: Inputs of different modalities can potentially substitute for one another to fire a granule cell.
source: Therefore, inputs of different modalities can potentially substitute for one another to fire a granule cell.
evidence: This is an inference based on the physiological properties of granule cells and their multimodal inputs.

claim: BPN neurons driven by cortical motor commands that do not directly participate in movement generation can be considered to carry corollary discharges by definition.
source: Since these BPN neurons will be driven by cortical motor commands that do not directly participate in movement generation, by definition they can be considered to carry corollary discharges.
evidence: This is an inference based on the anatomical connectivity and the definition of corollary discharge.

claim: Pontine corollary discharges may be processed similar to proprioceptive signals that synapse on the same granule cells.
source: Pontine corollary discharges will stimulate these granule cells, generate parallel fiber output to Purkinje cells, and may be processed similar to proprioceptive signals that synapse on the same granule cells.
evidence: This is a speculative inference about how convergent inputs might be processed.

claim: Hijacking the proprioceptive pathway could effectively convert the corollary message from motor to sensory coordinates.
source: Although speculative, hijacking this pathway could effectively convert the corollary message from motor to sensory coordinates, and thus in the appropriate reference frame to produce proprioceptive predictions.
evidence: This is explicitly labeled as speculative reasoning about a potential mechanism.

claim: Corollary discharge-driven predictions will contain some degree of error.
source: Corollary discharge-driven predictions will contain some degree of error, which is thought to be computed by comparing pure sensory models against forward models (Mazzoni and Krakauer, 2006; Shadmehr et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations and represents established theory about motor control.

claim: Areas containing granule cells where corollary and sensory information converge might represent components of forward models.
source: As described above, areas containing granule cells where corollary and sensory information converge might represent components of forward models.
evidence: This is a speculative inference about the functional role of convergent areas.

claim: Areas where proprioceptive streams are isolated from corollary/pontine information may represent what actually occurred and thus may drive pure sensory models.
source: Other areas where proprioceptive streams are isolated from corollary/pontine information may represent what actually occurred and thus may drive pure sensory models.
evidence: This is a speculative inference about the functional role of segregated areas.

claim: Common downstream targets of identified forward and sensory models may represent loci where intended and actual actions are compared and thus where error signals are generated.
source: Common downstream targets of these identified forward and sensory models may represent loci where intended and actual actions are compared and thus where error signals are generated.
evidence: This is a speculative inference about where error computation might occur.

claim: Corollary and sensory information has been shown to converge in the first stage of proprioceptive processing—in the precerebellar neurons of the spinal cord.
